From 9063d7e2615f4a7ab321de6b520e23d370e58816 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Massimiliano Pellizzer <massimiliano.pellizzer@canonical.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 15:30:50 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] apparmor: validate DFA start states are in bounds in
 unpack_pdb

Start states are read from untrusted data and used as indexes into the
DFA state tables. The aa_dfa_next() function call in unpack_pdb() will
access dfa->tables[YYTD_ID_BASE][start], and if the start state exceeds
the number of states in the DFA, this results in an out-of-bound read.

==================================================================
 BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in aa_dfa_next+0x2a1/0x360
 Read of size 4 at addr ffff88811956fb90 by task su/1097
 ...

Reject policies with out-of-bounds start states during unpacking
to prevent the issue.

Fixes: ad5ff3db53c6 ("AppArmor: Add ability to load extended policy")
Reported-by: Qualys Security Advisory <qsa@qualys.com>
Tested-by: Salvatore Bonaccorso <carnil@debian.org>
Reviewed-by: Georgia Garcia <georgia.garcia@canonical.com>
Reviewed-by: Cengiz Can <cengiz.can@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: Massimiliano Pellizzer <massimiliano.pellizzer@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>

diff --git a/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c b/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c
index 1769417a9962..ba5d40dbeb24 100644
--- a/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c
+++ b/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c
@@ -1010,7 +1010,17 @@ static int unpack_pdb(struct aa_ext *e, struct aa_policydb **policy,
 		if (!aa_unpack_u32(e, &pdb->start[AA_CLASS_FILE], "dfa_start")) {
 			/* default start state for xmatch and file dfa */
 			pdb->start[AA_CLASS_FILE] = DFA_START;
-		}	/* setup class index */
+		}
+
+		size_t state_count = pdb->dfa->tables[YYTD_ID_BASE]->td_lolen;
+
+		if (pdb->start[0] >= state_count ||
+		    pdb->start[AA_CLASS_FILE] >= state_count) {
+			*info = "invalid dfa start state";
+			goto fail;
+		}
+
+		/* setup class index */
 		for (i = AA_CLASS_FILE + 1; i <= AA_CLASS_LAST; i++) {
 			pdb->start[i] = aa_dfa_next(pdb->dfa, pdb->start[0],
 						    i);
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in AppArmor's policy unpacking code (in `security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c`).  
The DFA start states, read from untrusted binary policy data, were used as indexes into the DFA state tables without validation. The fix adds a bounds check on the start states before they are used.

#### Modifications in `security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c`:
1. **After unpacking the start state for `AA_CLASS_FILE`**, a new code block (lines 1010–1017) is inserted that:
   - Retrieves the number of states for the DFA (`state_count`) from the base table's `td_lolen` field.
   - Checks whether `pdb->start[0]` (the default start state) or `pdb->start[AA_CLASS_FILE]` exceeds `state_count`.
   - If any is out of bounds, an error string is set and the function jumps to the `fail` label, rejecting the malicious policy.

2. **Comment adjusted**: The original comment `/* setup class index */` now appears after the bounds-check block.

#### Relationships:
- The patch addresses a single vulnerability in one file (`policy_unpack.c`). The addition of the bounds check is directly related to the previously missing validation of start states.  
- The check prevents the subsequent usage of start states in `aa_dfa_next()` (which would cause the out-of-bounds read) by rejecting the policy early during unpacking.  
- The trivial comment movement preserves code clarity without affecting behavior.
